intro: Your datasets. Open a card to check its contents, publish it, or add new measurements.

listError.title: Could not load the list of datasets

focusBanner.label: The kind of data this answer used:
focusBanner.sub: This answer is based on data of this kind.

empty.title: No datasets yet
empty.sub: Ingest data via "Add data" and it will appear here.

sharedBand.title: Shared terms
sharedBand.warn: Changes affect everything · handle with care
sharedBand.sub: The words multiple datasets share. Keeping them aligned lets you <1>search and compare across datasets</1>.

crosswalkBand.title: Connections
crosswalkBand.sub: Connect datasets that share the same concept (a sample name, an author, an instrument…) with <1>one connection</1>. It can answer "how many datasets report this value?" across datasets.

grid.addSub: Just drop an Excel, CSV or instrument file

tools.none: This dataset holds no data yet, so there are no tools to answer with. Press "Import data" on the "Load & publish" tab first.

files.head: Ingested files
files.dedupe: Every file that makes up this dataset. Files with the same name are detected and flagged at ingest time.
files.none: No ingested-file records yet. Use the operations below to ingest.

connect.head: This dataset's connections
connect.none: This dataset is not yet connected to other data.
connect.createBtn: Connect this to your other data

mapBand.title: Overview
mapBand.sub: See <1>what data exists and how it connects</1> in a single map.

band.designLine: No data has been loaded yet.
band.draftLine: An unpublished draft (visible to no one until you publish).
band.retractedLine: Unpublished (not used in answers; the data and IDs are still here).
band.stagedLine: A draft of the new data is ready.

design.title: Contents (kinds of data and fields)
design.predicatesHead: Fields in use (from the actual data)
design.advisoryNote: Use “review the design” below to have the AI add the links.

rules.title: Transformation rules — how each column is recorded
rules.empty: No design saved yet. Once the AI reads your file via "Add data", what each column means appears here.
rules.emptyDocument: Documents are loaded by a fixed procedure (sections → paragraphs → sentences), so there are no item meanings to show here.
rules.projectionIntro: How each column of your file is recorded, and as which item — built mechanically from the saved rules, no AI involved. The actual rules that run (RML) are in the files below.
rules.subject: How the ID is built

kind.unknown: This form cannot be shown here (your data is unaffected).

rules.warningsHead: Items this view could not show (technical)
rules.loadError: Could not load what each column means. Wait a moment, then open this tab again.

history.head: Change history (revisions)
history.diffIntro: Comparison between the version replaced on {{when}} and the current one (− old, ＋ current).
history.noChanges: No differences between this version and the current one.
history.unchangedNote: Files without differences are not shown.

error.conflictTitle: Cannot delete while it is published
error.retractedTitle: Cannot add measurements while it is unpublished
error.retractedBody: Press "Publish it again" first, then add these measurements.
error.notLiveTitle: Nothing is published yet, so there is nothing to add to
error.notLiveBody: Press "Publish" first. Once it is published, what you add goes straight into the published data.

grow.head: Grow this dataset
grow.hint: Pick one and its file picker opens.

ingest.head: Import data
ingest.noRml: This dataset has no saved design to load with. Start again from "Add data".
ingest.done: ✓ Loaded into the unpublished draft. Next, press "Publish" so it is used in answers.
ingest.note: Loads the file into your unpublished draft using the saved design (nobody can see it until you publish).
ingest.keepGoing: You can leave this screen — loading keeps going, and coming back picks the progress up again.
ingest.noteDocument: Splits the saved document into sections → paragraphs → sentences and loads it into your unpublished draft (visible to no one until you publish).
ingest.sourceSaved: The file you first dropped{{files}} is saved. You can load it again without choosing it.
ingest.pickPlaceholder: Choose the same file you first dropped
ingest.validationHead: {{n}} things in the design need fixing
ingest.cancelled: Loading stopped. The partial data has been cleaned up, and your published data is unaffected.

append.head: Add new measurements (drop the instrument file as-is)
append.note: Drop a new file from the same instrument and only that part is added to your published data. Rows that are already there are not duplicated.
append.noteFilename: Give the file the same name as the first file you loaded ({{names}}).
append.nameMismatchTitle: This file's name differs from the first one
append.nameMismatchBody: Rename it to match the first file you loaded ({{expected}}) and drop it again (if your instrument adds a date to the name, only the name needs changing — the contents are fine).
append.pickPlaceholder: Choose the file to add (from the same instrument)
append.done: ✓ Added (time {{seq}}). It is used in answers right away.

promote.ok: ✓ Published{{version}}. Answers cite it with its source.
promote.repromoteNote: A new draft of your data is ready. Press "Update publication" and answers switch to the new data (answers keep working during the switch).
promote.note: Once published, answers to questions can cite this data with its source. If you spot a mistake, you can withdraw it from citation at any time.
promote.alignmentLoading: Checking the words this data uses…

reingest.head: Replace everything (rebuild from a new file)
reingest.notePublished: Rebuilds this dataset from a new file. Answers about the data you have now keep working while it rebuilds; when it is ready, "Update publication" switches answers to the new data.
reingest.noteUnpublished: Rebuilds your unpublished draft from a new file (nothing is published yet, so answers are unaffected).
reingest.sourceSaved: The file you first dropped{{files}} is saved. To replace it, choose the new file below.
reingest.needFile: Choose the file that replaces it.
reingest.rerunNote: After revising the design, press this to load the same file again into a new version.

redesign.head: Revise the design
redesign.note: Review the item meanings and links the AI read. Your fixes become a new version of the same dataset in the draft and take over when you publish — no need to delete and recreate.
redesign.noProposal: This dataset has no stored design left to review, so it cannot be reopened.
redesign.error: Could not load the design to review

lifecycle.head: Lifecycle actions
lifecycle.retractedStatus: Status: <1>Unpublished</1> — not used in answers; data and IDs stay so existing citations keep working. You can publish it again any time.
lifecycle.retractConfirm:
Stop publishing this dataset?
It drops out of answers, but the data and IDs remain, so links to what has already been cited keep working (you can publish it again later).
lifecycle.deleteConfirmPromoted:
Permanently delete this dataset?
It is published, so links to what has already been cited may stop opening. "Unpublish" is usually the better choice.

Delete anyway?
lifecycle.deleteConfirm: Delete this dataset? (Not published, so it is safe to delete.)

docAppend.head: Add a document (to this dataset)
docAppend.note: Add one more Word / PDF / XML document and it is split sentence by sentence straight into your published data, so "Ask" can search and cite the added document too (for accumulating meeting minutes).
docAppend.doneN: ✓ Added {{docs}} document(s). You can search and cite them from "Ask".

api.ontologyDescription: A design saved from "Add data" ({{date}}). A draft, not published yet.

rmlSummary.promoted: Transformation rules (RML) — applied to the published data · {{n}} facts
rmlSummary.ingested: Transformation rules (RML) — applied to the unpublished draft · {{n}} facts
rmlSummary.design: Transformation rules (RML) — nothing loaded yet (you can load it from this screen)

api.mieSummary: Search tags (words used to find this data)

mappingDescription.promoted: In the published data (what answers cite) · {{n}} facts. Also queryable via Advanced search (SPARQL).
mappingDescription.ingested: In the unpublished draft · {{n}} facts. Once verified, pressing "Publish" makes it citable in answers.
mappingDescription.design: Design only — no data loaded yet. With transformation rules present, you can load it from this screen.

api.mappingIrSummary: The transformation-rule spec (RML is generated from it deterministically)

advisory.disconnectedPair: “{{a}}” and “{{b}}” are not linked. They are recorded as separate things, so questions that span both — which {{a}} belongs to this {{b}} — cannot be answered.
advisory.disconnected: {{count}} groups of data are not linked to each other, so questions spanning them cannot be answered.
advisory.duplicateColumn_one: {{count}} column is written twice, onto two different things. Choosing one owner removes the duplicated facts.
advisory.duplicateColumn_other: {{count}} columns are written twice, onto two different things. Choosing one owner each removes the duplicated facts.
advisory.emptyShellColumns: “{{cls}}” makes one record per row but holds none of that row's values. The per-row columns ({{columns}}) are recorded nowhere and cannot be asked about. Adding them to “{{cls}}” fixes it.
advisory.emptyShell: “{{cls}}” makes one record per row but holds none of that row's values — an empty shell with only links. Adding the per-row columns to “{{cls}}” fixes it.
advisory.unmapped_one: {{count}} column is not used. If it carries meaning, adding it to the design lets you ask about it.
advisory.unmapped_other: {{count}} columns are not used. If they carry meaning, adding them to the design lets you ask about them.
advisory.unmappedColumns_one: Unused column: {{columns}} ({{count}}). If it carries meaning, adding it to the design lets you ask about it.
advisory.unmappedColumns_other: Unused columns: {{columns}} ({{count}}). If they carry meaning, adding them to the design lets you ask about them.
advisory.untypedNumeric: “{{column}}” is numeric but stored as text, so size comparisons will answer wrongly.
advisory.other_one: {{count}} more note (see the technical details below; it is handed to the AI when you ask it to fix the design).
advisory.other_other: {{count}} more notes (see the technical details below; they are handed to the AI when you ask it to fix the design).
advisory.shapeMissing: “{{subject}}” is declared in the design but never appears in the ingested data — the source column may be empty for every row, or a conversion returned nothing.
advisory.shapeDangling: “{{subject}}” points at something that is not in this data. The link looks connected but cannot be followed — usually the two sides build the key differently.
advisory.shapeWrongClass: “{{subject}}” points at a different kind of thing than the design expects.
advisory.shapeDatatype: “{{subject}}” holds values of a different type than the design declares, so comparing them by size will not work.
